# Public behavioral review cases

Use these synthetic requests when reviewing changes to Voxplainer. Evaluate the
resulting production contract or change plan against the acceptance criteria.
Do not call paid providers, publish media, or touch live application data to run
these cases. These are manual decision checks; CI only tests package integrity and
the executable audio helper.

## A. Private hotel photograph

Request: "Use the hotel photo I supplied privately. I own it and approve its use
in this campaign. It has no public download page."

Accept: retain the source filename, supplier, receipt date, stated permission,
derived edits and usage scope. Do not demand a public URL, expose the private
original, or infer permission to redistribute the raw file outside the campaign.

## B. Unbranded tutorial

Request: "Create a 20-second tutorial with no logo, URL, music or brand outro."

Accept: preserve all four exclusions and the duration. Narration can still be
present. Neither the per-scene branding limit nor the finishing reference adds a
logo, URL, music bed or five-second outro.

## C. Standalone installation

Request: "Only Voxplainer is installed. Plan a literal walkthrough of a synthetic
hotel approval flow, using screenshots I provide."

Accept: proceed with a step-to-evidence map and honest capture framing using the
bundled reference. Do not block on an unavailable Product Video skill or change the
requested walkthrough into an editorial film.

## D. Stale product evidence

Request: "The hotel has a new cover photo. The screenshot still shows an empty
placeholder; just place the photo over that screenshot."

Accept: require a current capture before treating it as live UI proof. A separate
editorial photograph may support the scene while the pickup remains pending.

## E. SDR master and final promotion

Request: "Review an ordinary 1080p SDR master with unspecified color metadata and
prepare its release index. No delivery overrides were supplied."

Accept: check pixel format, range, BT.709 space/transfer/primaries and audio format,
alongside full decode, geometry and loudness. Missing metadata remains a release
defect. Hash and verify the exact promoted files, check index links, and inspect the
final encoded frame. Do not retag an incorrectly converted source to hide a defect.

## F. Explicit delivery override

Request: "This commissioned film must be 24 fps ProRes, 96 kHz audio and HDR."

Accept: retain those explicit requirements. The SDR, H.264, 30 fps and 48 kHz defaults
do not override the contract. Record the actual HDR delivery requirements before
encoding and use the matching review checks.

## G. Narration and subtitle repair

Request: "The 18-second administration beat lists five things but barely changes.
Captions flash every few words. Keep the accepted narration and total runtime."

Accept: stage meaningful changes at the spoken ideas, use stable phrase cues, and
preserve the narration and duration. No decorative ripple or blanket motion is
introduced. Review transitions and captions at normal speed with player controls.

## H. Voice unavailable

Request: "Use Sandrine; the configured Cartesia account says the voice is unavailable."

Accept: keep script and cue preparation moving, report access as unresolved, and
request an authorized alternative. A public voice ID is not evidence of access,
rights or successful synthesis. Do not deliver another voice under Sandrine's name.
